worldViewer.deleteChunksBody: Their entries are blanked in the region header, which is how Minecraft itself forgets a chunk. The server regenerates them from scratch the next time a player goes near. Anything built there is gone.
worldViewer.description: BlueMap’s live map, the world’s level.dat, and the region grid, read straight off the server’s own files.
worldViewer.emptyBody: A world appears here once the server has generated one. Start it up, or upload a world folder into the server root.
worldViewer.nbtSaved: {{file}} saved. The old copy is beside it as {{file}}_old.
worldViewer.noBlueMapBody: BlueMap ships one build per platform, and none of them matches this server.
worldViewer.noBlueMapTitle: No BlueMap build for this server
worldViewer.noLevelBody: This world has no readable level.dat. It may still be generating, or the node may be offline.
worldViewer.noRegionsBody: This world has no region files yet. Nothing in it has been generated, or it is not a Java world.
worldViewer.openFailed: That file could not be opened.
worldViewer.regionFailed: That region could not be read.
worldViewer.reinstallHint: Click to reinstall the newest build.
worldViewer.saveFailed: That file could not be saved.
worldViewer.title: World Viewer
worldViewer.windowBlocked: Your browser blocked the map window. Allow pop-ups for this panel and try again.
worldViewer.windowBody: The map is the owner's, so it opens in a window of its own instead of inside the panel.

discordBot.title: Discord Bot
discordBot.heroGlobal: Control your servers from Discord. Link your account once and every command runs as you, with exactly the permissions you have here.
discordBot.heroPersonal: Run your own bot. Choose which commands it has, who in your Discord may use each one, and how its messages look.
discordBot.loadFailed: The Discord bot settings could not be loaded.

link.title: Your Discord account
link.description: The bot needs to know which Discord is yours before it will act for you.
link.oauthHint: You sign in on Discord itself, so only the Discord account you prove you own can ever reach your servers.
link.popupHint: Finish in the window that opened. It closes itself once Discord sends you back.
link.notReady: Linking is not set up yet
link.notReadyBody: An administrator still has to finish connecting the bot. Check back soon.
link.keyRevokedBody: The API key the bot used for you was deleted, so it can no longer act for you.
link.unlinkBody: The bot stops acting for you straight away, its API key is deleted, and any alerts you set up stop.
link.blocked: The browser blocked the Discord window. Allow pop-ups for this site and try again.
link.taken: That Discord account is already linked to a different panel account.
link.mismatch: You were signed out while linking. Sign in and try again.

install.title: Add the bot
install.description: Add it to your own Discord account to use the commands anywhere, or to a server so it can post alerts there.

commands.title: Commands
commands.descriptionGlobal: What this bot can do. Type / in Discord to see them.
commands.rolesFailed: Your bot's Discord roles could not be loaded.
commands.noServers: Add your bot to a Discord server to pick roles from it.
commands.rolesBody: Anyone with one of these roles can use /{{command}}. You can always use it yourself.
commands.actionsLast: At least one has to stay on.

command.servers: Every server you can reach, with live status and resources.
command.controlpanel: Live console, resources and power controls for one server.
command.power: Start, stop, restart or kill a server.
command.command: Send a command to a server's console.
command.backups: Create, lock, unlock, download and delete backups.
command.connect: Addresses, subdomains and SFTP details for a server.
command.activity: The latest things that happened on a server.
command.billing: Plan, price, renewal date and unpaid invoices for a server.
command.alerts: Ping a role when a server runs hot or goes down.
command.account: Which panel account the bot is acting as.
command.unlink: Disconnect this Discord account from the panel.

access.title: Full access
access.description: These Discord accounts can use every command, just like you, acting as your panel account. Only add people you trust with your servers.
access.pending: Checked with Discord when you save
access.hint: In Discord, turn on Developer Mode under Settings, Advanced, then right-click someone and choose Copy User ID. Anyone the bot turns away is also shown their ID.
access.invalid: A Discord user ID is 17 to 20 digits.
access.isOwner: That account already owns the bot.
access.full: You can add up to {{count}} people.

design.title: Design
design.accentHint: The stripe down every card. Empty follows the panel accent.
design.visibilityHint: Who can see command replies. "Let users pick" adds a private option to each command.
design.consoleStyleHint: An image colours timestamps, levels, addresses and errors, and reads the same in light and dark Discord.
design.barLengthHint: Squares in each resource bar. Longer bars fill a wide screen but wrap sooner on a phone.
design.bannerHint: A banner on the control panel and on /help.
design.logosHint: The game's logo beside each server.

studio.saved: Saved. Discord picks up command changes within a minute.
studio.saveFailed: Those changes could not be saved.
studio.previewFailed: The preview could not be drawn.

own.setupDescription: Everybody on this panel runs their own bot. Yours only ever acts as you.
own.step1: Create an application. Its name and icon are what people see.
own.step2: Open Bot, press Reset Token and copy the token.
own.step3: Paste it below. The application ID and public key are read from Discord for you.
own.step4: Paste the Interactions Endpoint URL this page then shows into General Information, and save.
own.tokenPlaceholder: Paste the token from the Bot page
own.connected: Bot connected. Now paste its endpoint URL into the Developer Portal.
own.connectFailed: That bot could not be connected.
own.endpointHint: Paste into General Information in the Developer Portal. Discord saves it once the panel answers its test.
own.syncFailed: Discord would not take the commands.
own.removeBody: The bot stops answering, its API key is deleted, and its alerts stop. The application itself stays in the Developer Portal.
own.keyRevoked: Your bot's API key was deleted, so it cannot act for you. Sync the commands to issue a new one.

alerts.title: Alerts
alerts.description: Set up in Discord with /alerts add, and checked every minute.
alerts.emptyBody: In your Discord server, run /alerts add, then pick a server and a role to ping.
alerts.removeBody: The bot stops posting about this server in that channel.
alerts.removeFailed: That alert could not be removed.

servers.title: Servers in Discord
servers.description: Hidden servers don't show up in /servers or as you type, and the bot won't open, control or send alerts for them.
servers.saveFailed: That change could not be saved.

server.title: Discord
server.readyBody: Run any command below in Discord to manage this server. Its ID is {{id}}.
server.linkBody: Link your Discord account to start and stop this server, read its console and handle backups from Discord.
server.personalBody: Set up your own bot first. It then works on this server with the permissions you have here.
server.actsAsYou: The bot acts as your panel account, with exactly the permissions you have on this server.
server.commandsBody: Copy one of these into Discord. The server is already filled in.
server.alertsBody: Pings in Discord when this server runs hot or goes down.
server.alertsEmpty: In your Discord server, run /alerts add server:{{id}} and pick a role to ping.
server.previewBody: Drawn from this server right now, in your bot's design.
